findings.question: q-physics-waves-and-sound-0004
findings.problem: The keyed choice is the only bare category name; every distractor adds a reason or condition. Across these classification items, this repeated choice form lets a student select the short label without classifying the wave.
findings.fix: Give every choice the same structure, such as a category followed by a brief reason.

findings.question: q-physics-waves-and-sound-0005
findings.problem: The keyed choice is the only bare category name, while all three distractors say Mechanical and add a reason or condition. This repeats the answer-form cue in question 0004 and allows selection by presentation rather than wave knowledge.
findings.fix: Use parallel category-and-reason choices with comparable wording.

findings.question: q-physics-waves-and-sound-0006
findings.quote: Wavelength is the distance over which a periodic wave repeats its phase. Adjacent crests are one wavelength apart.
findings.problem: The explanation relies on the technical terms periodic and phase without explaining them. A Grade 5 reader who does not already understand phase gets no plain-English account of why this distance is wavelength.
findings.fix: Say: Wavelength is the distance from one crest to the next crest. It measures the length of one complete wave.

findings.question: q-physics-waves-and-sound-0007
findings.quote: Longitudinal because particles return to equilibrium
findings.problem: Two choices name Longitudinal, and returning to equilibrium also occurs in a longitudinal wave. If that category were correct, both longitudinal choices would fit. A test-wise student can eliminate that category from the choice overlap, while Transverse is the lone bare alternative to the obviously implausible no-orientation claim.
findings.fix: Use distinct, parallel descriptions of motion, without repeating the same classification in two choices.

findings.question: q-physics-waves-and-sound-0008
findings.problem: The keyed answer is the only bare category label without a competing choice of the same category. Transverse appears twice, once with an added amplitude condition, and the remaining choice rejects compressions as disturbances. This repeats the classification answer-form cue in questions 0004, 0005, and 0007.
findings.fix: Make all choices parallel and distinct; remove the pattern of a bare correct label versus qualified distractors.

findings.question: q-physics-waves-and-sound-0018
findings.quote: Which statement about sound speed is supported by the lesson?
findings.problem: Referring to the lesson makes the stem sound like a classroom reading check rather than a standalone CET science question. The item needs no lesson reference to be answered.
findings.fix: Ask: Which statement about the speed of sound is correct?
